List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Sandeep Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Sunil Kumar,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Criminal Case No. 7702 of 2021, Case Crime No. 379 of 2020, under Sections 376, 323, 328, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Kaptanganj, District Kushinagar, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have established corporeal relationship with the victim on the false promise of marriage and had later on refused to comply with the said Irshad Ali vs State Of U.P. on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57522770/
1 promise.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
There is no clinching evidence to suggest that the applicant misled the victim from the beginning.
The informant has converted a failed consensual physical relationship into a criminal case.
There is no previous criminal history of the applicant except the case u/s 174 IPC instituted subsequent to the instant FIR.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 15.10.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application but has not disputed the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the applicant.

7. In the case of Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648, the Supreme Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused by itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. The Supreme Court in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and Another, 2019 (9)
SCC 608 and Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 886, has stated that entering into any kind of corporeal relationship with a person on the false promise to marry cannot be termed as rape.

entities.text:
Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and Another, 2019 (9)
SCC 608

entities.text: Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 886

sentences.text: 9. This Court has avoided expressing its opinion as the case hinges on whether the applicant's promise of marriage was genuine or false and whether the physical relationship was consensual or not.
It is for the Trial Court to draw a conclusion which will depend on the evidence presented before it and its interpretation as per law.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant- Irshad Ali who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S. 12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
